Sabores de Hidalgo

Site Plan · Gastronomía tradicional de Hidalgo, México

Project Overview

This document is the planning stage for a basic website about the traditional food of Hidalgo, Mexico. The final website will explore representative dishes, their cultural origins, and the regions where they are prepared. The design uses a colorful visual direction inspired by Tenango embroidery and the colorful tablecloth shown in the project reference image.

Planned navigation: Home · Dishes · History & Culture · Share Your Recipe · References

1. Site Name

Sabores de Hidalgo

Possible domain: saboresdehidalgo.com

I chose this name because it is simple, memorable, and immediately communicates the main subject of the website: the traditional flavors and culinary heritage of Hidalgo. The name also leaves room to discuss different regions, ingredients, dishes, and family traditions.

Logo concept

The logo uses the initials SH inside a circular plate-like shape, with small decorative stars inspired by the colorful, handmade feeling of Tenango embroidery. The final logo can later be replaced with a more detailed food/folk-art symbol.

2. Site Purpose

The site will document and introduce the traditional gastronomy of Hidalgo, Mexico. It will provide accessible information about representative dishes, ingredients, cultural influences, historical background, and the regions where different foods are prepared.

The project will especially highlight the influence of Otomí and Nahua traditions, the state's mining history, and the geographic diversity of Hidalgo, from the Valle del Mezquital and mining region to the Sierra and Huasteca.

Planned content

  • Home: visual introduction, regional overview, and featured dishes.
  • Dishes: barbacoa, pastes, mixiote, ximbó, escamoles, zacahuil, trout, apple ate, and other regional foods.
  • History & Culture: Indigenous roots, mining influence, geography, ingredients, and culinary traditions.
  • Share Your Recipe: an HTML form for visitors to submit a family recipe or comment.
  • References: sources for facts and external images used in the final website.

3. Scenarios

Scenario 1: “I am visiting Hidalgo. Which traditional dishes should I try, and what region are they associated with?”
Scenario 2: “Where did pastes come from, and how are they connected to the mining history of Real del Monte?”
Scenario 3: “I have a family recipe from Hidalgo. Where can I share it or learn more about its regional origins?”

4. Color Schema

The palette uses vivid colors inspired by Tenango-style Mexican folk art and the colorful food presentation in the reference image. The bright colors will contrast with photographs of food while the cream and dark brown tones keep the page readable and grounded.

Magenta — headings & primary accents #D81B60
Turquoise — navigation, links & secondary accents #008F95
Yellow — highlights, buttons & decorative elements #F4C430
Coral — important accents & visual emphasis #E6533C
Cream — main page background #FFF8E7
Dark brown — body text, footer & contrast #3B2418

Visual reference provided for the project: colorful Mexican-inspired food presentation and textile pattern.

5. Typography

Bree Serif — headings and site title

This font gives the project a warm, handmade, food-focused personality while remaining easy to read for headings.

Poppins — body text, navigation, labels, and form content

Poppins provides a clean and modern contrast to the decorative heading font. It will be used for paragraphs and most interface elements.

Font sources: Google Fonts. Fallback fonts will be used if the web fonts cannot load.
